title: Infer launch heuristics engine + telemetry refactor to cut cold-start latency
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Problem: Cold-starts on heterogeneous GPU pools (mixed SMs, drivers, and quantized kernels) are a significant contributor to tail latency for short requests. We currently probe kernels and do on-demand linking in the main runtime path which increases request latency and noisy startup patterns. This ticket refactors kernel selection/launch decisioning out of the hot path into a separate heuristics engine and restructures telemetry to drive deterministic prewarming decisions. Goals: 1) Reduce median and P95 cold-start token latency for short sequences by eliminating synchronous kernel probe/link operations in the request path. 2) Provide a lightweight heuristics engine that consumes aggregated telemetry (model id, sequence-length histogram, preferred kernel variant, last-run success) and outputs a per-instance prewarm plan. 3) Make kernel selection deterministic and reproducible by recording a short signed manifest of chosen kernels per model-version for rollback/diagnostics. 4) Keep runtime changes minimal and backward compatible with existing fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: No synchronous kernel symbol probing in the request hot path; probes moved to heuristics prewarm or background workers
Median cold-start token-latency reduced by >=20% for targeted short-request workloads in perf lab
Heuristics engine exposes an API for (model_version) -> (prewarm_plan) and a CLI for forced prewarm
Signed kernel selection manifests are emitted for every model-version rollout and surfaced in Console rollouts tab
Automatic fallback still works when preferred kernel fails (graceful degrade to compatible variant)
tasks: Design heuristics engine API and in-memory cache schema
Refactor telemetry pipeline: add seq-length histogram summaries and last-success tags
Implement background prewarm worker (sidecar-style) that applies prewarm_plan per instance
Emit signed kernel-selection manifest and store in artifacts service
Update runtime to consult local prewarm cache and avoid blocking probes
Add integration tests in perf lab and a canary rollout plan
Instrument Console to show kernel manifests and prewarm status per-instance
risks: Incorrect heuristics may prewarm many kernels and increase memory/GPU footprint
Telemetry lag could lead to stale prewarm plans for sudden workload shifts
Signed manifests add an extra artifact path that must be hardened for private deployments
Rolling this out without careful canarying could regress tail latency for some fleets
implementation_notes: Initial prototype uses existing telemetry ingestion (promtail -> clickhouse) and adds a lightweight summarizer job that emits per-model sequence-length histograms every 5m. Heuristics are rule-based initially (thresholds derived from perf lab), with a plan to replace with an ML scorer later. Prewarm worker will live as a non-blocking thread in the instance process with strict CPU/GPU quotas; if constraints disallow prewarm it will fall back to requesting the prewarm API on a colocated helper pod. Manifests are JSON blobs signed by release-key and stored alongside model artifacts.
